headline: ByteDance and Tencent are speeding up work on personal AI agents that act for their users after the success of Meta's Muse, Caixin reports.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: Caixin's own sourcing, backed by Global Times and the South China Morning Post on the trend, but it rests on one unnamed company source and the paywalled article gives no launch dates or features.
importance_line: What changed is that two of China's biggest internet companies are racing to build assistants that carry out tasks for people rather than only chat, which could reach users of apps such as ByteDance's Doubao, but Caixin cites one company source and no launch date, features or price are known.
summary: Caixin reports, citing a company source, that ByteDance sped up work on a personal AI agent (software that carries out tasks for its user) for its Doubao phone assistant before China's early-October National Day holiday, building on a project code-named "Spell" begun in April, and that Tencent is also fast-tracking one, as both chase the success of Meta's Muse. Muse launched on 8 September and passed 2.5 million downloads in two weeks, the South China Morning Post reports, while Bank of America's Winnie Wu told it that China's closed app ecosystems and users' reluctance to pay subscriptions may make the model harder to copy there.
notes: Only the first two paragraphs of the Caixin Global article were readable (paywall); context from Global Times (https://www.globaltimes.cn/page/202610/1372021.shtml) and the South China Morning Post as carried by The Star. Global Times says Caixin first reported this on Friday 9 Oct 2026 in Chinese; the English Caixin Global article is dated 12 Oct 2026. Related to yesterday's Ant Group LingGuang 2.0 item (1011:C02-03) and the nanoMuse item (1011:C02-16).
